draft.title: Material living standards
card: Material living standards are about how much people can get of the goods and services they use. Food, housing, clothing, transport and healthcare services are examples.
Higher incomes usually let people buy more and better goods and services. So material living standards tend to rise when incomes rise.
They are often measured by real GDP per person. Real GDP is the value of output with price rises removed. Dividing by population shows the output for each person on average.
Real GDP per person is an average. It lets us compare a country over time, or compare countries of different sizes.
draft.remember: Material living standards are about access to goods and services, and real GDP per person is a common measure.

a.q: Which change would most directly show a rise in a country's material living standards?
opts: Real GDP per person rises over several years
Total real GDP rises while the population rises faster
Prices of goods and services rise by 5% in a year
The population of the country grows by 2% in a year
a.why: Real GDP per person rising means more output for each person on average, so access to goods and services is rising. Total real GDP can rise while output per person falls, if the population grows faster.
a.clue: Look for the measure that is both real and per person.

b.q: Country X has real GDP of $500 billion and 10 million people. Country Y has real GDP of $900 billion and 30 million people. What can be said about their material living standards?
opts: X is higher, as its real GDP per person is greater
Y is higher, as its total real GDP is greater
They are equal, as both countries have a large real GDP
Y is higher, as it has more people to work
b.why: Country X has $50,000 per person and Country Y has $30,000 per person. Material living standards are measured per person, so X is higher. Y's larger total is tempting, but it is shared among three times as many people.
b.clue: Divide each real GDP by its population before comparing.

a.best: Real GDP per person rises over several years

b.best: X is higher, as its real GDP per person is greater
